summary: Both coin counts are capped at 100, the accepted solution uses a fixed arithmetic formula, and every legal game has at most 25 forced turns; the complete 10,000-pair domain is too small for an honest runtime-scaling verdict.

replacement_checks.evidence: The value equation has the unique nonnegative solution of one 75-value coin and four 10-value coins per turn; the accepted implementation computes min(x, floor(y / 4)) and its parity with fixed arithmetic.
The certificate regression checks all 10,000 legal ordered (x, y) pairs against an independent turn-by-turn simulator that removes one 75-value coin and four 10-value coins until no move remains.
